title: EKS Orchestrator Terraform module for Private control plane: upgrade-guard + health probes
creator: Priya Nair
description: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (module: redwood_eks_orchestrator) that provisions the Private control-plane EKS stack with built-in upgrade safety: preflight probes, staged/blue-green upgrade orchestration, automatic rollback hooks, and health-checking primitives for both control-plane and nodegroup changes. This module should be compatible with cross-account KMS key rotation, external-dns annotations used by private ingress controllers, and produce standardized outputs for Redwood's Private reconciler. It must support immutable, idempotent deploys and expose toggles for canary batch sizes and parallelism to meet latency and SLA constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives under modules/eks_orchestrator and is published to our private registry with versioning
Module exposes inputs for upgrade strategy: manual | canary | blue-green and canary_batch_percent (1-50)
Preflight validation step runs a set of API/endpoint probes before changing control-plane IAM or nodegroup AMI/launch template

Automated rollback trigger: if health probes (control-plane API, kube-system pod readiness, and sample inference pod) fail during canary, the module records a plan and reverts infrastructure changes within 5 minutes
Module integrates with our KMS cross-account aliases and supports optional key rotation window parameter
End-to-end test harness passes in CI: create cluster (ephemeral), run canary upgrade with induced failure, assert rollback occurred and cluster state restored
Documentation and runbook published: inputs/outputs, upgrade workflow, SLO impact matrix, and operator remediation steps
tasks: Design Terraform schema: inputs/outputs and lifecycle rules
Implement preflight IAM and API probes using local-exec and null_resource hooks where necessary
Add blue-green orchestration primitives using nodegroup tagging + traffic-shift marker resources
Implement automated rollback using remote-exec + Lambda-actuated apply reversal (if enabled)
Wire in KMS alias handling (cross-account) and add rotation window input
Create CI job in infrastructure pipeline to run ephemeral cluster tests
Write user-facing docs + operator runbook and add to private-deploy handbook
Security review: coordinate with Security for KMS usage and IAM least-privilege
comments: 2025-02-12 Priya Nair: Initial ticket created after RFC-priv-eks-upgrades (link in Links). Goal is to avoid past incidents where upgrades caused long rollbacks and customer-visible errors.

2025-02-14 Diego Alvarez: Spike completed for preflight probes. Using a lightweight Go binary to run sequence of checks is feasible; can also run kubeclient queries from CI. Next: prototype canary batch workflow using nodegroup tags.

2025-02-18 Maya Chen (SRE): Reviewed proposed probes. Add a TTL-based quorum check for kube-system pods and a synthetic inference request against rtp-test model to catch model-serving regressions. Also: ensure metrics emitted to Prometheus for alerting during upgrade windows.

2025-02-20 Diego Alvarez: Implemented blue-green test harness in feature branch feature/eks-orchestrator-upgrade-guard. Created GH PR #2897. Early tests show controlled nodegroup creation and traffic shift marker works, but rollback path for control-plane API changes needs better reconciliation logic.

2025-02-23 Security review kickoff: Security requested explicit KMS alias rotation policy and proof that no long-lived credentials are created during module runs. Assigned to Priya to provide docs and min-priv policy templates.
2025-02-25 QA run: CI ephemeral cluster test failed when induced failure relied on a 60s timeout. Increased probe timeout and added exponential backoff; re-running.
2025-02-26 Diego Alvarez: Updated ticket with new due date and added canary_batch_percent default 10%. Marking PR as ready for review pending Security sign-off.
decision_log: 2025-02-13: Decided to implement upgrade strategies in the module instead of relying on external orchestrator to reduce operator complexity (decision by eng + sres)
2025-02-16: Chose nodegroup tagging blue-green pattern over full cluster replacement to minimize time to rollback and preserve PV attachments
2025-02-19: Agreed to make automated rollback opt-in (default: enabled for internal environments, disabled for customer-managed runs) pending legal review
2025-02-22: Opted for Lambda-actuated rollback triggers to avoid requiring long-lived credentials on the module runner; Security approved approach with ephemeral role assumption
notes: Implementation should avoid module-level null_resource executions where possible; prefer resource-based lifecycle and remote state locks
Consider adding a feature flag to switch between Terraform-driven orchestration and a controller (k8s operator) if complexity grows
Measure upgrade duration and error-rate before/after for each tenant and expose metrics to Console by default
